leftEvidence.title: Remember Jesus Christ, risen and descended from David

points.label: Action and response
points.left: The letter commands remembrance of Jesus raised from the dead and descended from David, joins that gospel to imprisonment, endurance for the chosen, a faithful saying, and God’s faithfulness.
points.right: The argument holds promise of entering rest, creation’s seventh day, wilderness unbelief, Joshua, and a later day designated through David’s “Today,” then urges diligence.

points.label: Evidence boundary
points.left: The source places Davidic descent appears inside a compact remembrance shaped by resurrection and endurance inside this David setting without explaining every motive, transition, or later consequence.
points.right: The source places David locates a later speaking of “Today” inside an argument spanning creation and wilderness inside this David setting without explaining every motive, transition, or later consequence.

payload.posture: 2 Timothy 2:8–13 and Hebrews 4:1–11 are distinct approved David Scenes in the authored “Gospel and Apostolic Memory” movement; holding them together exposes what continues and what changes without collapsing their sources.

rightEvidence.title: A later “Today” is located in David

payload.tension: 2 Timothy 2:8–13 foregrounds Davidic descent appears inside a compact remembrance shaped by resurrection and endurance; Hebrews 4:1–11 foregrounds David locates a later speaking of “Today” inside an argument spanning creation and wilderness. Their sequence does not by itself explain every change between them.
